base_lists

Base lists: short names, long paths, wrapping, collisions, and supertraits.

Legend

  • A type prints as a C++ declaration: class when its body starts with an internal or private member and struct when it starts public, with the members of all its impls merged in.
  • static marks a function with no receiver; () mut marks one that takes &mut self, and a method with no marker takes &self.
  • : Clone, Debug is the base list: the standard traits a type derives or implements, by short name.
  • A type lists its data first, its fields or variants, then its other members. internal: opens the pub(crate) members, private: the rest, and public: goes back to public; a label prints only where the access changes from what the keyword gives, so a type can show one twice.
  • A module's item that is not public gets // internal or // private above it.
  • [[...]] is an attribute that shapes the API or its wire format, such as [[must_use]] or [[serde(rename = "id")]].
  • implements: Trait for Type; is an impl with no declared type to attach to, such as a blanket impl.
  • MACRO marks a macro definition, an invocation, a derive from another crate, or an attribute macro.
  • A doc comment prints as prose, and backticked text prints in the code font; a member's comment reflows as one paragraph.

MACROS: 1 derive list

  • MACRO derive: From, in Wrapped

globbed::Starred

Marker

A unit struct whose list fits on the head line.

struct Marker : Debug, Eq, Hash

Ordered

Standard derives that are not special members, and comparisons with another type written by hand. The crate's own Clone trait never sits on the shared line, so the standard Clone keeps its short name.

struct Ordered(u8)
    : Clone, Eq, Ord, PartialEq, PartialEq<u8>, PartialOrd, PartialOrd<u8>

other::Foreign

The other crate's Display, which stays apart from the standard one.

struct Foreign
    : other_crate::Display

Plain

Standard supertraits and a lifetime bound.

{
}

Renamed

The standard Display through a renaming use.

RunError

The crate's Error makes std::error::Error keep its full path.

}

A class with a standard trait.

Sink

Two traits named Write keep their full paths.

struct Sink : std::fmt::Write, std::io::Write

Spelled

The standard Display written in full, with no use.

Spellings

  • std::fmt::Debug is written 2 ways; prefer Debug, which is not used yet:
    • Dbg, once
    • fmt::Debug, 4 times
  • std::fmt::Display is written 4 ways; pick one and search for the rest:
    • D, once
    • Display, once
    • fmt::Display, 5 times
    • std::fmt::Display, once
